Tools in biomechanics report two kinds of data. Some data come from direct readings. Other data come from math models, tuning, or signal filters. This hub points to articles that look at those layers. A summary here describes the linked article. It does not give new proof for that page.

::: {.callout-important}
## State and Editorial Contract

**Available** means you can read the linked article. It does not mean every claim on the page is proven. Each article must show what is measured, derived, or modeled. It must state its sources and its limits. Read each page for its own findings and tests.
:::

## Measurement Guides

### [Force Measurement Technology](../articles/technology-force-measurement.html)

**Article state: Available.** Covers force plates, pressure mats, wrenches, and centers of pressure. It looks at setup rules and tool limits. Check the article page for device details and test rules.

### [Motion Capture Technology](../articles/technology-motion-capture.html)

**Article state: Available.** Covers cameras, markers, and body sensors. It looks at axes, calibration, and error sources. This hub does not call any camera setup accurate for all tasks.

### [Launch Monitor Technology](../articles/technology-launch-monitors.html)

**Article state: Available.** Covers radar and camera systems. It separates direct sensor readings from calculated club and ball numbers. Tool accuracy depends on the unit, firmware, and test setting.

### [Launch Monitor Vendor Reference](../articles/launch-monitor-vendor-reference.html)

**Article state: Available.** Lists public maker manuals and word meanings. It is a source guide, not an endorsement. It does not prove that two tools measure the same thing in the same way.

## Modeling and Analysis Guides

### [Club Fitting Simulation and Parameter Identification](../articles/technology-club-fitting.html)

**Article state: Available; engineering workflow experimental.** Explains club model changes, shaft bend, and swing weights. Computer results depend on the model, chosen numbers, and test bounds.

### [Multibody Impact Coupling and the Heavy Hit Hypothesis](../articles/technology-heavy-hit-impact-coupling.html)

**Article state: Available; hypothesis scope model-conditioned.** Examines short impact times, shock waves, and linked bodies. Read the math and limits before using any finding in coaching.

### [The Reference-Point Problem in Club Delivery Data](../articles/reference-point-problem.html)

**Article state: Available.** Shows how clubhead speed depends on the point chosen on a turning clubface. Math examples depend on the chosen setup and shape.

### [Impact Mechanics and Ball Flight](../articles/impact-mechanics-and-ball-flight.html)

**Article state: Available.** Surveys strike and flight models, their inputs, and their differences. Model outputs are math results, not real player swings.

### [Rotation-Induced Spin](../articles/rotation-induced-spin.html)

**Article state: Available; bounded model result.** Computes ball spin from a turning clubface under rigid contact rules. Physical outcomes depend on whether those rules fit the actual strike.

### [The Physics of the Rolling Putt](../articles/putting-roll-models.html)

**Article state: Available.** Builds simple models for strike, skid, roll, slope, and cup capture. Course slopes and green speeds limit all model forecasts.

### [Simulating the Green](../articles/green-simulation.html)

**Article state: Available; software and stochastic extensions experimental.** Shows how to code roll equations, ball events, surfaces, and green slope in software. Simulated makes are not proven human make rates.

## Shared Geometry, Bounded

Twist and wrench math offers a shared language for motion and load readings. Their product gives mechanical power when axes align. That math pairing does not make every sensor a full six-axis tool. Sensors have different limits, ranges, and model needs. Each tool must be checked on its own.
